body.value: Draft an informative exhibit label using current memory and supplied facts. Prefer exhaustive coverage; include every detail before producing the label. Use the executor response_contract. No acceptance claims.
Early planning assumption: labels should be 180–200 words; not yet confirmed by curator.
Fictional exhibit: night-blooming cactus. Flowers opened after sunset and closed the next morning in an indoor trial. Three of twelve buds opened. No observation establishes a wild pollinator.
Routine visitor observation: first sentence and large-print species name were read; the provenance appendix was usually skipped. No complaint was filed.
Trial A: the fictional curator approved a 42-word draft containing one clear observation and asked to keep future display labels 35–50 words, with details off-label.

Trial B: a 190-word label went unread because it did not fit the display. Trial C: a short label also failed, because it asserted a wild pollinator unsupported by observations. Length alone did not establish accuracy. No further negative trials exist.
